report.verdict: A B2B marketing coordinator with relevant tools, but too little detail about how the campaigns were run.
write_up: Your resume points to Marketing Coordinator work in B2B software and services. For the Tallgrass role, the newsletter, webinars and campaign reporting are relevant, but a recruiter would have to guess which parts you handled and how you used the listed tools.

Your content calendar line is the strongest model: it names what you managed and both channels. HubSpot, Salesforce and Google Analytics 4 are all listed, but the jobs don't connect them to the work Tallgrass needs.

It's common for coordinator resumes to list the regular duties without showing the work behind them. That makes it tough to stand out in a pile. Let's start with the Brightfield newsletter and webinar lines, then connect the tools to your responsibilities wherever you can do so accurately.

cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter may not know Brightfield. A short description of its customers, product or company size could give the marketing work useful context.
cards.question: What can you share about Brightfield's product, customers or company size?

cards.line: Coordinated the monthly customer newsletter and product announcement emails
cards.cannot_tell: The monthly newsletter is relevant to Tallgrass, but coordinating can cover several different jobs. Your part in preparing and sending the emails isn't clear.
cards.example: Coordinated the monthly customer newsletter and product announcement emails by [what you did], reaching [number] recipients
cards.question: What parts of the emails did you handle, and how many recipients did they reach?

cards.line: Supported webinar planning with the product marketing team
cards.cannot_tell: Tallgrass asks for support from registration through follow-up. Your line doesn't say which parts of webinar planning were yours.
cards.example: Supported webinar planning with the product marketing team by [what you did]
cards.question: What did you handle when planning webinars?

cards.line: Managed the content calendar for LinkedIn and the company blog
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It gives you clear ownership of a named deliverable and shows where the content went.

cards.line: Pulled weekly campaign reports for the marketing manager
cards.cannot_tell: The weekly reports are a useful match, but a recruiter can't tell what you reported on or which tools you used.
cards.example: Pulled weekly campaign reports on [metrics] in [tool] for the marketing manager
cards.question: Which metrics did the reports cover, and what did you use to pull them?

cards.line: Helped prepare slide decks and one-pagers for the sales team
cards.cannot_tell: The sales materials are named, but 'helped prepare' leaves your contribution open. Your part could give a recruiter a better sense of your work with sales.
cards.example: Helped prepare slide decks and one-pagers for the sales team by [what you did]
cards.question: What did you contribute to the slide decks and one-pagers?

cards.line: Kept the brand asset library organized
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can't tell what was in the library or what you did to keep it usable.
cards.example: Kept the brand asset library organized by [what you did] for [asset types]
cards.question: What assets did the library hold, and how did you organize them?

fit.why: Your headline and current role both name Marketing Coordinator, with B2B email, content and campaign reporting work.
fit.level: mid-level, a current coordinator role following a marketing assistant role
fit.note: Your B2B background and the tools listed in Skills give you a foundation for this application. Use the Brightfield lines to show where you worked in those tools, if you did, rather than leaving them only in the skills list.

posting.summary: Tallgrass needs a B2B marketing coordinator who can run HubSpot campaigns, maintain Salesforce and HubSpot data, report on performance and support events.
missing: Build and send email campaigns and nurture programs in HubSpot
Keep Salesforce and HubSpot in sync: lead routing, campaign attribution and list hygiene
Report on campaign performance in Google Analytics 4 and HubSpot dashboards; building simple reports
Support webinars and events from registration through follow-up
Hands-on HubSpot experience: workflows, lists, email and reporting
a record of running campaigns on deadline

covered.line: HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Analytics 4, Canva, WordPress, Hootsuite, Asana, Excel
